column3: “Then I looked and saw” recasts “and I looked and behold.”
“Sound” renders φωνὴν (“voice”); “strumming” renders “harping.”
BSB leaves out “as” (ὡς) before “a new song”; “sang” renders the present “are singing.”
BSB has no “by Jesus” (Ἰησοῦ). “They follow” leaves out “these are those.”
BSB follows the critical text with “lie” and no “before the throne of God,” which the Textus Receptus has.
“Overhead” renders μεσουρανήματι (“mid-heaven”).
Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text with “a second angel,” “Babylon the great” (no “city”), and “who”; BSB leaves out “another” (ἄλλος). “Passion” renders θυμοῦ (“wrath”).
BSB leaves out “another” (ἄλλος) before “a third angel.”
“Poured” renders “mixed.”
“There is no rest for” recasts “they have no rest.”
BSB follows the critical text with no second “here” and adds “a call for.”
BSB has “telling me to write,” with “me” as in the Textus Receptus; the critical text has no “to me.” “From this moment on” renders “from now.”
Close to the Greek.
“Swing” renders πέμψον (“send”); “is ripe” renders “has dried up.”
“Swung … over” renders “cast … upon.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text with “loud voice.” “The clusters of grapes” renders “the clusters.”
“The grapes of the earth” renders “the vine of the earth.”
“Rose as high as” renders “as high as.”
